'''Christopher Joseph Schofield''' (also known as Chris Schofield) is a Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name=":22">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.ox.ac.uk/people/chris-schofield|title=Christopher Schofield|publisher=University of Oxford|access-date=2023-07-24}}</ref> and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]. Chris Schofield is a professor of [[organic chemistry]] at the [[Chemistry Research Laboratory, University of Oxford|University of Oxford, Department of Chemistry]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://schofield.chem.ox.ac.uk/|title=Home – Schofield Group|publisher=University of Oxford|access-date=2016-08-08}}</ref> and a Fellow of [[Hertford College, Oxford|Hertford College]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hertford.ox.ac.uk/about/people/professor-chris-schofield-frs|title=Professor Chris Schofield FRS {{!}} Hertford College|publisher=University of Oxford|access-date=2016-08-08}}</ref> Schofield studied functional, structural and mechanistic understanding of [[enzyme]]s that employ oxygen and [[Alpha-Ketoglutaric acid|2-oxoglutarate]] as a co-substrate.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Chowdhury|first1=Rasheduzzaman|last2=Sekirnik|first2=Rok|last3=Brissett|first3=Nigel C.|last4=Krojer|first4=Tobias|last5=Ho|first5=Chia-hua|last6=Ng|first6=Stanley S.|last7=Clifton|first7=Ian J.|last8=Ge|first8=Wei|last9=Kershaw|first9=Nadia J.|date=19 June 2014|title=Ribosomal oxygenases are structurally conserved from prokaryotes to humans|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=510|issue=7505|pages=422–426|doi=10.1038/nature13263|issn=0028-0836|pmc=4066111|pmid=24814345|bibcode=2014Natur.510..422C}}</ref> His work has opened up new possibilities in [[Antibiotics|antibiotic]] research,<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last1=Hamed|first1=Refaat B.|last2=Gomez-Castellanos|first2=J. Ruben|last3=Henry|first3=Luc|last4=Ducho|first4=Christian|last5=McDonough|first5=Michael A.|last6=Schofield|first6=Christopher J.|date=10 December 2012|title=The enzymes of β-lactam biosynthesis|journal=Natural Product Reports|language=en|volume=30|issue=1|doi=10.1039/C2NP20065A|issn=1460-4752|pages=21–107|pmid=23135477}}</ref> oxygen sensing,<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Schofield|first1=Christopher J.|last2=Ratcliffe|first2=Peter J.|date=1 May 2004|title=Oxygen sensing by HIF hydroxylases|journal=Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology|language=en|volume=5|issue=5|pages=343–354|doi=10.1038/nrm1366|pmid=15122348|s2cid=6586977|issn=1471-0072}}</ref> and [[Regulation of gene expression|gene regulation]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite journal|last1=Thinnes|first1=Cyrille C.|last2=England|first2=Katherine S.|last3=Kawamura|first3=Akane|last4=Chowdhury|first4=Rasheduzzaman|last5=Schofield|first5=Christopher J.|last6=Hopkinson|first6=Richard J.|date=1 December 2014|title=Targeting histone lysine demethylases – Progress, challenges, and the future|journal=Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Gene Regulatory Mechanisms|series=Methylation: A Multifaceted Modification – looking at transcription and beyond|volume=1839|issue=12|pages=1416–1432|doi=10.1016/j.bbagrm.2014.05.009|pmc=4316176|pmid=24859458}}</ref>

After work on plant and microbial [[oxygenase]]s,<ref name=":3" /> he studied uncharacterised human oxygenases.<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Horita|first1=Shoichiro|last2=Scotti|first2=John S.|last3=Thinnes|first3=Cyrille|last4=Mottaghi-Taromsari|first4=Yousef S.|last5=Thalhammer|first5=Armin|last6=Ge|first6=Wei|last7=Aik|first7=WeiShen|last8=Loenarz|first8=Christoph|last9=Schofield|first9=Christopher J.|date=7 April 2015|title=Structure of the Ribosomal Oxygenase OGFOD1 Provides Insights into the Regio- and Stereoselectivity of Prolyl Hydroxylases|journal=Structure|volume=23|issue=4|pages=639–652|doi=10.1016/j.str.2015.01.014|pmc=4396695|pmid=25728928}}</ref> His research has identified unanticipated roles for [[oxygenase]]s<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal|title=Structural Basis for Binding of Hypoxia-Inducible Factor to the Oxygen-Sensing Prolyl Hydroxylases| doi=10.1016/j.str.2009.06.002 | volume=17|issue=7 |journal=Structure|pages=981–989|pmid=19604478|date=July 2009 | last1 = Chowdhury | first1 = R | last2 = McDonough | first2 = MA | last3 = Mecinović | first3 = J | last4 = Loenarz | first4 = C | last5 = Flashman | first5 = E | last6 = Hewitson | first6 = KS | last7 = Domene | first7 = C | last8 = Schofield | first8 = CJ|author7-link=Carmen Domene| doi-access = free }}</ref> in regulating [[gene expression]], importantly in the cellular [[Hypoxia (medical)|hypoxic]] response,<ref name=":9">{{Cite journal|last1=Hon|first1=Wai-Ching|last2=Wilson|first2=Michael I.|last3=Harlos|first3=Karl|last4=Claridge|first4=Timothy D. == Education ==
Chris Schofield attended [[St Anselm's College]] catholic [[grammar school]] in Merseyside, then studied for a [[Bachelor of Science]] in [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Manchester]] and graduated with a first class honour (1979–1982). In 1982, he moved to [[Oxford]] to study for a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] with Professor [[Jack Baldwin (chemist)|Jack E. Baldwin]]. In 1985, he became a Departmental Demonstrator in the [[Dyson Perrins Laboratory]], [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] followed by his appointment as a Lecturer in [[Chemistry]]<ref name=":0" /> and a [[Fellow]] of [[Hertford College, Oxford|Hertford College]]<ref name=":1" /> in 1990. In 1998, he became professor of [[Chemistry]],<ref name=":22"/> and in 2011 he was appointed the Head of Organic Chemistry<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://selectbiosciences.com/conferences/biographies.aspx?conf=ewc2012&speaker=100755|title=SELECTBIO – Epigenetics Speaker Biography|website=SELECTBIO|access-date=2016-08-08}}</ref> at the [[Department of Chemistry, University of Oxford|Department of Chemistry]], University of Oxford. In 2013, he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]], FRS.<ref name=":11">{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/christopher-schofield-12241/|title=Christopher Schofield|publisher=royalsociety.org|access-date=2016-08-08}}</ref>

== Research ==
The work in laboratory of Chris Schofield focuses on different areas of research, including:

=== Molecular Mechanisms of the Hypoxic Response ===
[[Hypoxia-inducible factors|Hypoxia-inducible factor-1]] (HIF-1) is a heterodimeric α,β-transcriptional complex<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wilkins|first1=Sarah E.|last2=Abboud|first2=Martine I.|last3=Hancock|first3=Rebecca L.|last4=Schofield|first4=Christopher J.|date=19 April 2016|title=Targeting Protein–Protein Interactions in the HIF System|journal=ChemMedChem|language=en|volume=11|issue=8|pages=773–786|doi=10.1002/cmdc.201600012|issn=1860-7187|pmc=4848768|pmid=26997519}}</ref> that mediates the cellular response to oxygen availability in multi-cellular organisms,<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Jaakkola|first1=Panu|last2=Mole|first2=David R.|last3=Tian|first3=Ya-Min|last4=Wilson|first4=Michael I.|last5=Gielbert|first5=Janine|last6=Gaskell|first6=Simon J.|last7=Kriegsheim|first7=Alexander von|last8=Hebestreit|first8=Holger F.|last9=Mukherji|first9=Mridul|date=20 April 2001|title=Targeting of HIF-α to the von Hippel-Lindau Ubiquitylation Complex by O2-Regulated Prolyl Hydroxylation|journal=Science|language=en|volume=292|issue=5516|pages=468–472|doi=10.1126/science.1059796|issn=0036-8075|pmid=11292861|bibcode=2001Sci...292..468J|s2cid=20914281|doi-access=free}}</ref> ranging from the simplest known animal ''[[Trichoplax|Trichoplax adhaerens]]'' to humans.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5"/><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Epstein|first1=Andrew C. === Structural and Functional Studies on 2OG Oxygenases ===
The [[2-oxoglutarate (2OG)-dependent dioxygenases|2-oxoglutarate (2OG)-dependent oxygenases]] are a superfamily of non-haem iron dependent [[2-oxoglutarate (2OG)-dependent dioxygenases|oxygenase]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Clifton|first1=Ian J.|last2=McDonough|first2=Michael A.|last3=Ehrismann|first3=Dominic|last4=Kershaw|first4=Nadia J.|last5=Granatino|first5=Nicolas|last6=Schofield|first6=Christopher J.|date=1 April 2006|title=Structural studies on 2-oxoglutarate oxygenases and related double-stranded β-helix fold proteins|journal=Journal of Inorganic Biochemistry|series=High-valent iron intermediates in biologyHigh-valent iron intermediates in biology|volume=100|issue=4|pages=644–669|doi=10.1016/j.jinorgbio.2006.01.024|pmid=16513174}}</ref> most of which use the [[Citric acid cycle|Krebs cycle]] intermediate, [[Alpha-Ketoglutaric acid|2OG]], as a [[cosubstrate|co-substrate]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Welford|first1=Richard W.D.|last2=Kirkpatrick|first2=Joanna M.|last3=McNeill|first3=Luke === Antibiotics: Biosynthesis and Resistance Mechanisms ===
Most clinically used [[antibiotics]] are based upon [[natural product]]s.<ref name=":4" /> The most important family of antibiotics contains a [[Beta-lactam|β-lactam]] ring, and includes the [[penicillin]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=van Berkel|first1=Sander S.|last2=Nettleship|first2=Joanne E.|last3=Leung|first3=Ivanhoe K. The group's biosynthetic work has focused on the [[clavam]]s<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mackenzie|first1=Alasdair K.|last2=Valegård|first2=Karin|last3=Iqbal|first3=Aman|last4=Caines|first4=Matthew E.
